purpose: Public synthetic state-transition fixtures extending the rejected-input preservation contract at PR #130; no runtime, host, model or validation execution results.
identity_unknown_reason: No host/model experiment is part of S011. Requested authoring-chat speed does not establish the server tier; host, platform and model observations are unavailable.
scope: One fresh in-memory DecisionSession per sequence with fixed canonical bundle/projections at source_sha; response_policy=None as in DecisionChecks.setUp. All steps within a sequence share that instance. Native hooks, active installs, legacy selector and actual application are outside this fixture.
synthetic_input_rule: All contexts, decision IDs, feature envelopes and fault values are authored synthetic values. Explicit method requests are stipulated fixture inputs, not inferred user preferences. No prompt/transcript/host-log data is included.

notation.request: A literal JSON request. Only a one-key $response object is substituted before handle; booleans remain booleans. No implicit merge or repair.
notation.states: Named full snapshots of scope,last_key,last_selection,last_reason,delivered,available,busy. scope/last_selection are JSON-array encodings of Python tuples. available is an unordered set of [identity,digest] pairs.
notation.pre_state: Assert the named snapshot immediately before the step; no direct state seeding. Reach it only by running prior steps in order.
notation.response_subset: Assert every supplied leaf and exact array lengths; unspecified object keys are unconstrained. Resolve expectation operators before comparison.
notation.$response: Step ID plus # plus RFC 6901 JSON Pointer into its actual response, sequence-local only. Requests may reference only prior responses; post-state assertions may also reference the response just returned. A null/missing digest or reason capture, or a failed referenced step, is a failure, never a guessed value.
notation.$request_sha256: sha256(json.dumps(resolved_request, sort_keys=True).encode()).hexdigest(), exactly matching decision.py; use Python default separators and ensure_ascii=True. This is an expectation formula, not a captured hash.
notation.$canonical_instructions: Complete ProjectionInstructionAssembler instructions for the stated method/locale/revision from the fixed canonical source pair. No instruction content is stored as an observed result.
notation.$canonical_sha256: sha256: prefix plus SHA-256 of UTF-8 canonical instructions for the specified method/locale/revision.
notation.post_state: Assert the named snapshot after handle has returned, including busy=False. Exact membership of delivered/available is required, not only counts.
notation.scope_assertion: For every valid select response, also require response.scope to equal that step request context/epoch; selected methods must retain applied=unverified.
notation.not_a_runner: This is an S011-local draft fixture notation. No tool currently consumes this file. Mapping it to a runner requires integration-owner approval and implementation outside S011 ownership.

fault_preserves_state.claim: RequestFault returns a repairable response without calling _reset; finally releases busy.

fault_response.claim: Closed field/error/repair metadata extends the fail-open failure response.

initial_and_reset_state.claim: Initial volatile fields; busy starts false.

reset_state.claim: Reset clears scope, last selection key/reason, delivered and available.

catalog_metadata.claim: Catalog validates locale and returns metadata without mutating volatile state.

acknowledge.claim: Acknowledgment adds only previously delivered digests in the exact current scope; read/availability are agent assertions.

scope_validation.claim: Scope checks precede mutation; only a fully valid new context/epoch invokes reset.

select_validation.claim: Envelope, scope, decision, revision, locale, participation and routing validation all precede _scope.

selection_cache.claim: Exact sorted-JSON request hash reuses the last selection; new accepted requests replace the last cache even for no_intervention.

delivery_inventory.claim: Delivery identity binds method, locale and content revision; only acknowledged exact identity/digest pairs suppress instructions.

routing_shape.claim: Unsupported answer shape rejects before selection.

routing_features_shape.claim: Missing routing keys and non-list features are input faults.

explicit_and_mechanical.claim: Mechanical participation returns no route; eligible explicit methods select their exact identity.

documented_contract.claim: One process retains volatile state; rejected requests do not change session state; availability assertions do not prove application.

cli_stream_lifetime.claim: One run_decision stream owns one session; one-shot calls create separate sessions.

routing_reason_values.claim: Router reason values are explicit_method and no_eligible_method for these stipulated explicit and mechanical inputs.

duplicate_exclusions.exclusion: Do not copy its 20 standalone mutation cases, IDs or historical fictional task. Six different fault shapes here are only triggers for new multi-step state assertions.
Do not add independent happy-path reuse, revision reopen, repeat-without-ack, compaction or process-freshness cases.
Do not add independent locale, reset, compound selection or multi-method inventory cases.
Do not reproduce stale-epoch/recursion, one-error repair, fault-matrix or state-label-only tests.
Do not reproduce changed recommendations, cross-question examples or the error-free stream boundary.

unresolved.topic: Runtime or packaged-content failure after request acceptance
unresolved.reason: RequestFault preservation does not establish transactional rollback for _scope/_deliver failures after acceptance; not exercised or asserted here.

unresolved.topic: Malformed JSON stream, oversized input, EOF or process restart
unresolved.reason: These are CLI/process boundary behaviors outside the direct handle sequences. No additional CLI guarantee is inferred from the six sequences.

unresolved.topic: Host read, semantic application and utility
unresolved.reason: Acknowledged is an agent assertion; fixture authorship/execution cannot authenticate host receipt, complete agent read, reasoning application or better answers.
S001 has not frozen the integrated SHA for this fixture. No executable adapter or candidate validation is owned or run by S011.

sequences.title: 동일 요청 정정 후 선택 캐시와 acknowledge 보존 / Preserve cached selection and acknowledgment after same-request repair
sequences.novel_assertion: After a revision-type rejection, the corrected original request must reuse both the last routing selection and the acknowledged digest. A metadata query between correction and requery must preserve both.
sequences.overlap_exclusion: Excludes standalone revision-type validation. Existing repair test starts with no acknowledged success; reuse/catalog tests have no intervening rejected select.

sequences.title: 거부된 다음 epoch와 승인된 다음 epoch / Rejected versus accepted next epoch
sequences.novel_assertion: A valid higher epoch with a later routing error must leave old availability intact. Only its corrected accepted form retires the old assertions; unacknowledged repeats must keep emitting.
sequences.overlap_exclusion: Excludes the existing successful compaction and stale-epoch assertions. The new assertion is the unchanged complete snapshot before a later-field invalid epoch advance is repaired.

sequences.title: 거부된 새 context와 정정 후 인계 / Rejected new context followed by corrected handoff
sequences.novel_assertion: A syntactically valid different context with negative revision must not retire the acknowledged Korean inventory until the request is fully repaired; the accepted handoff must emit afresh.
sequences.overlap_exclusion: Excludes the existing error-free context-change test. This sequence checks both sides of the validity boundary using a Korean acknowledged state.

sequences.title: 오류와 정정을 거친 EN/KO 전달 재조회 / EN and KO availability across rejection and repair
sequences.novel_assertion: A rejected Korean request leaves the acknowledged English identity untouched; corrected Korean delivery needs its own acknowledgment. Returning to English retains its bytes despite a different last routing key.
sequences.overlap_exclusion: Excludes the existing locale-digest distinction test and ordinary reuse test; neither asserts an acknowledged locale inventory through a rejected cross-locale select.

sequences.title: 여러 선택의 availability와 마지막 캐시 분리 / Separate accumulated availability from the last selection cache
sequences.novel_assertion: A routing-key rejection after two acknowledged distinct decisions must preserve the complete two-method inventory and the last request key; revisiting either decision changes only the last cache.
sequences.overlap_exclusion: Excludes standalone missing-key checks and successful multi-method inventory checks. The new assertion is both identities and the exact last cache surviving an intervening malformed select.

sequences.title: 유효한 빈 선택과 이후 오류가 기존 availability에 미치는 영향 / Empty selection and later rejection preserve prior availability
sequences.novel_assertion: After acknowledgment, a valid mechanical no_intervention replaces the last cache without clearing delivered/available identities. A rejected negative epoch must preserve that empty cache; correction and later substantive requery retain their distinct outcomes.
sequences.overlap_exclusion: Excludes the existing isolated mechanical gate and mechanical-to-reasoning tests. This sequence binds a prior acknowledged identity, an empty success, a rejected select, repaired empty reuse and later retained substantive delivery.
